author: Mark Atwood
text:
Filing 'human' because the bead's primary fix (bump Cargo.toml from 0.1.1 to 0.1.2) is mechanically a one-line edit but is governed by workspace release-engineering policy that isn't codified in AGENTS.md.

Findings from workspace audit:

1. Per-crate patch bumps DO happen — jmap-server and jmap-mail-server are already at 0.1.2 (commit 0a0dc73, 2026-05-05). The workspace does not require all 30 crates to bump in lockstep.

2. Workspace Cargo.toml dep constraint is 'version = "0.1"' (caret-major) so 0.1.2 still satisfies. No constraint-update needed.

3. Workspace Cargo.toml comment (lines 55-59) explicitly says: 'Use version = "0.1" (caret-major) so any 0.1.x release of a sibling satisfies the constraint; bump to version = "0.2" workspace-wide when the coordinated 0.2 API-break beads (JMAP-g7wu.1 CallerCtx, JMAP-g7wu.3 helpers builder, JMAP-g7wu.9 UTCDate, JMAP-r3pg.14 extract_account_id) land together.' So the *next coordinated bump* is planned to be 0.2.0, not 0.1.2.

4. The recent jmap-types changes (extras propagation, State newtype migration) are not RFC-spec-breaking and are wire-compatible, BUT they break downstream String-typed bindings (per bd:JMAP-6xs8.6, closed with migration recipes added). External crates.io consumers pinning to jmap-types 0.1.1 will silently get the new behavior if a crate they depend on bumps and pulls jmap-types 0.1.2 via the 'version = "0.1"' constraint.

5. CHANGELOG.md does not exist (bd:JMAP-6xs8.22). A version bump without a CHANGELOG entry has nothing for consumers to point at to understand 'what changed in 0.1.2'.

Recommendation: bump jmap-types 0.1.1 → 0.1.2 simultaneously with .22 (CHANGELOG creation) so the bump and the CHANGELOG entry land together. If .22 is deferred indefinitely, alternatively, defer the bump too — it doesn't matter for the workspace dep constraints (still 0.1.x) until either crates.io publish or a coordinated 0.2.0 cut.

Rationale for not autonomously bumping:
- Bumping without CHANGELOG creates an opaque version on crates.io.
- The maintainer may have a specific plan for the next coordinated publish event.
- Bumping just jmap-types is asymmetric with the State migration's downstream consumers (jmap-base-client, every extension client) that ALSO consume the migrated types but stay at 0.1.1.

Awaiting maintainer direction on the publish-strategy question.
